content:
Andy Robertson, a Liverpool defender, has emphasized the importance of strengthening the team's defensive line to support new manager Arne Slot in his inaugural season, particularly as they prepare to face Manchester United this Sunday. Liverpool has had a commendable start to the season, securing two clean sheets in their opening matches against Ipswich and Brentford. However, the game against Manchester United is expected to pose a more significant challenge.

handle the defensive issues effectively will be crucial for Liverpool, especially considering their performance last season. The team conceded 41 goals in 38 games, finishing third in the league. This record was notably poorer than that of the champions, Manchester City, who conceded only 34 goals, and the runners-up, Arsenal, who conceded 29. Robertson acknowledged the need for improvement, stating, "When you look back at last season’s stats, I think even when we were still in the title race, we were conceding more chances probably than Arsenal and Man City. And when you do that, there’s going to be a game where you get punished."

Robertson expressed optimism about the team's current form, highlighting the two clean sheets as an ideal start. He stressed the importance of maintaining this momentum, saying, "We hope that we can keep that going and we hope that we can limit Man United to the chances. And after the international break we hope we can limit all the other teams to chances." The defender's comments underscore the team's commitment to tightening their defense to avoid the pitfalls of the previous season. By focusing on reducing the number of chances conceded to opponents, Liverpool aims to enhance their competitive edge and secure a stronger position in the league.

P.S. The article suggests that Liverpool's defensive performance will be a critical factor in their success this season, especially under the new management of Arne Slot. The team's ability to limit opponents' scoring opportunities will be crucial in their upcoming match against Manchester United and throughout the season.
